items.text: The case-sensitive email lookup in `BlockedEmail.should_block?` creates a bypass risk, allowing 'User@Example.com' to bypass a block on 'user@example.com'. This can lead to unauthorized access to blocked users.

BlockedEmail.should_block? mutates state (match_count/last_match_at) and is called from email validation which can run multiple times per request (e.g., user.valid? then user.save), inflating stats and causing extra writes for a single signup attempt

should_block? is a predicate method but has write side effects (increments match_count, sets last_match_at, saves record), violating command-query separation; callers expect a ? method to be a pure read but every invocation silently mutates the database
BlockedEmail.should_block? should use email.downcase when querying to ensure case-insensitive matching
Extra blank lines at start/end of describe block in email_validator_spec.rb violate RuboCop Layout/EmptyLinesAroundBlockBody convention

Blocking applies to any email change not just signup: change_email never checks blocklist and sends confirmation to blocked address, then EmailToken.confirm hits RecordInvalid, rescues it and returns nil giving user generic token failure with no reason
User.create_for_email and EmailToken.confirm never record blocked attempts due to transaction rollback behavior
Regex pattern should be changed from @(#{domains}) to @(?:#{domains})\z to anchor domain matching to end of string
User.new_from_params assigns params[:email] raw with no downcase, strip, or before_validation hook, and Email.downcase exists but is unused

Any server-side email error including 'has already been taken' and domain whitelist/blacklist adds the address to rejectedEmails, showing generic user.email.invalid text instead of the server's reason; list persists until page reload preventing retry of unblocked addresses
Letter case bypasses the email block - BlockedEmail.where(email: email) is case-sensitive, so blocked emails can be bypassed with different casing (e.g., Bad@spammers.org bypasses bad@spammers.org)

pushObject(result.values.email) will add null/undefined if the server response omits values.email or returns it blank, leaving a non-string entry in rejectedEmails - should ensure value is present before caching
BlockedEmail model needs email normalization via before_validation callback to downcase emails before storage
No updated specs for the modified User model validations
Normalize the email before querying in BlockedEmail.should_block?; otherwise blocked addresses can be bypassed by changing case

BlockedEmail.should_block? writes match_count/last_match_at from inside validation, causing block stats to be wrong: increments are rolled back when validation fails in save/save!, so blocked attempts via User.create_for_email and EmailToken.confirm are never counted; UsersController#create counts only because of separate user.valid? call before user.save; :do_nothing matches are counted twice per signup (valid? + save)
UsersController#create now returns user.errors.to_hash which could potentially leak internal validation details

BlockedEmail.should_block? performs a database write (updating match_count and last_match_at) during a validation callback, which is an unusual side-effect pattern that could have subtle implications when validation is called without intending to persist
Counter update uses read-modify-write pattern (record.match_count += 1; record.save) causing lost increments under concurrent signups - should use atomic update_all
match_count/last_match_at increment for :do_nothing matches while commit says it tracks how many times each address is blocked

EmailValidator spec stubs BlockedEmail.should_block? (a class the patch owns) and no integration or controller test covers the blocked-signup path, stats persisting through real User#save, case handling, or new errors/values JSON keys - violates 'never mock things you own' rule
'last_match_at is null' example tests an ActiveRecord/migration default not app logic - tests framework code rather than application behavior
Regex in email_in_restriction_setting? missing end anchor allows suffix domain bypass - user@example.com.evil.com matches whitelisted example.com domain
email_validator.rb file is missing a trailing newline
No updated specs for the changes to UsersController#create

BlockedEmail.should_block? has a write side-effect (incrementing match_count and saving) that executes every time validations run, causing match_count to be incremented by 2 per registration attempt instead of 1 because user.valid? is called explicitly and then user.save triggers validations again
BlockedEmail.should_block? performs a case-sensitive SQL query on PostgreSQL, allowing users to bypass blocked email checks by varying case (e.g., Bad@SpamClub.COM when bad@spamclub.com is blocked)
File has no trailing newline while every other file in the repo ends with a newline
File has no trailing newline

The regex pattern @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? method only matches domain suffixes, not full domains with proper boundary anchoring. An attacker can register evil.example.com to bypass a whitelist entry for example.com.
Email.downcase() only lowercases the domain part, not the local part, so using it won't fix the case-sensitivity issue - need to use full downcase instead

email_in_restriction_setting? calls value =~ regexp which will raise if value is nil (e.g., missing email param) even though presence validation would already fail - need to guard validate_each / email_in_restriction_setting? against blank/nil values
EmailValidator no longer rejects malformed email addresses, so validates :email, email: true can now accept values like sam@sam or sam
No controller spec covers the new errors and values keys in users#create failure JSON (lines 198-199)
Case-sensitive email lookup in BlockedEmail.should_block? creates bypass risk - User@Example.com can bypass a block on user@example.com

The computed property depends on rejectedEmails.@each but @each is mainly for observing per-item properties and can be unreliable for array membership changes with primitive items like strings - may not recompute when pushObject is called depending on Ember version
Domain whitelist/blacklist uses case-insensitive regex but blocked email check is case-sensitive, creating inconsistent behavior
Counter update uses non-atomic read-modify-write pattern (match_count += 1; save), causing concurrent attempts to lose increments; save return value is ignored and save re-runs the uniqueness SELECT
Any server-side email error adds address to rejectedEmails including 'has already been taken', showing generic 'invalid' message instead of actual error reason
EmailValidator spec stubs BlockedEmail.should_block? instead of testing real validator-to-model boundary, hiding case-sensitivity and counter defects
blocked_email_spec.rb only uses lowercase emails, missing test coverage for case variants
Invite redemption to a blocked email (User.create_for_email with save!) raises an unhandled ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid

Changing email to a blocked address fails silently - change_email doesn't check blocklist, sends confirmation to blocked address, and EmailToken.confirm rescues RecordInvalid returning nil with generic token failure message
should_block? increments match_count and last_match_at inside validation, and users#create validates twice (user.valid? then user.save), causing double counting for do_nothing matches
Block lookup is case-sensitive with no normalization, so changing letter case bypasses the block (bad@spammers.org blocked but Bad@spammers.org or bad@SPAMMERS.org allowed)
rejectedEmails list persists until page reload, preventing retry of addresses unblocked in the meantime
Return value of save is ignored in counter update

BlockedEmail.should_block_email? method has side effects during a read operation - it updates statistics even when just checking if an email should be blocked. This could cause race conditions in concurrent environments and makes the method name misleading.
Potential duplicate entries in rejectedEmails array if user submits same blocked email multiple times
Blocked-attempt stats are lost on rollback - Rails 3.2.12 save runs validations inside with_transaction_returning_status which rolls back when validation fails, undoing BlockedEmail increments
:do_nothing action type (enum, NOT NULL action_type column, set_defaults callback, fabricator line, two spec contexts) has no producer in the patch - no admin UI, caller or setting
Missing regression test covering nil/blank value when whitelist/blacklist settings are present to ensure validation doesn't raise unexpectedly
Consider using the new user.email.blocked translation key instead of user.email.invalid for blocked email validation messages
values: user.attributes.slice('name','username','email') is redundant: client reads only values.email which equals the email it already submitted since new_from_params does not normalize

issues.claim: BlockedEmail.should_block? looks up the email case-sensitively (BlockedEmail.where(email: email)) with no normalization, so a blocked address can be bypassed by changing letter case (e.g. Bad@spammers.org vs bad@spammers.org). This is also inconsistent with the case-insensitive domain whitelist/blacklist regex.

BlockedEmail.should_block? increments match_count/last_match_at inside email validation, and users#create runs validations twice (user.valid? then user.save), so one signup attempt is counted twice and causes extra writes.
should_block? is a predicate/validation-time method with write side effects: it increments match_count, sets last_match_at and saves the record on every call.

Blocked-attempt stats written during validation are rolled back when save/save! fails validation inside its transaction, so blocked attempts via User.create_for_email and EmailToken.confirm are never recorded.
The match_count update uses a non-atomic read-modify-write (match_count += 1; save), so concurrent attempts lose increments.
The return value of save in the counter update is ignored.
The regex @(#{domains}) in email_in_restriction_setting? lacks boundary/end anchoring, so addresses with domains that extend a whitelisted domain (e.g. user@example.com.evil.com) match the whitelist.
email_validator.rb is missing a trailing newline.
Extra blank lines at the start/end of the describe block in email_validator_spec.rb violate RuboCop Layout/EmptyLinesAroundBlockBody.
change_email does not check the blocklist and sends a confirmation to a blocked address; EmailToken.confirm then rescues RecordInvalid and returns nil, giving a generic token failure with no reason.
Redeeming an invite to a blocked email via User.create_for_email (save!) raises an unhandled ActiveRecord::RecordInvalid.
User.new_from_params assigns params[:email] raw with no downcase/strip or before_validation hook, and the existing Email.downcase is unused.
Email.downcase lowercases only the domain part, not the local part, so it does not remove case sensitivity of the blocked-email lookup.

On the client, any server-side email error (including 'has already been taken' and domain whitelist/blacklist) adds the address to rejectedEmails, which then shows the generic user.email.invalid text instead of the server's reason.
The rejectedEmails list persists until page reload, so addresses unblocked in the meantime cannot be retried.
pushObject(result.values.email) adds null/undefined to rejectedEmails when the server response omits or blanks values.email.
The computed property depends on rejectedEmails.@each, which may not recompute on pushObject of primitive string items.
Submitting the same blocked email multiple times adds duplicate entries to rejectedEmails.
UsersController#create now returns user.errors.to_hash, exposing internal validation details.
match_count/last_match_at are incremented for :do_nothing matches, while the commit says it tracks how many times each address is blocked.
The :do_nothing action type (enum, NOT NULL action_type column, set_defaults callback, fabricator, spec contexts) has no producer in the patch: no admin UI, caller or setting.
email_in_restriction_setting? evaluates value =~ regexp, which raises when value is nil (e.g. missing email param); validate_each does not guard against blank/nil values.
There is no regression test for a nil/blank value when whitelist/blacklist settings are present.
EmailValidator no longer rejects malformed addresses, so validates :email, email: true accepts values like sam@sam or sam.
Blocked-email validation uses the user.email.invalid translation key instead of the new user.email.blocked key.

values: user.attributes.slice('name','username','email') in the failure JSON is redundant: the client reads only values.email, which equals the submitted email because new_from_params does not normalize.

The EmailValidator spec stubs BlockedEmail.should_block? (a class the patch owns) instead of exercising the real validator-to-model path, and no integration test covers the blocked-signup path, stats persistence, or case handling.
The 'last_match_at is null' example tests an ActiveRecord/migration default rather than application logic.
blocked_email_spec.rb uses only lowercase emails and has no tests for case variants.
The modified User model validations have no updated specs.
There are no updated specs for UsersController#create, including the new errors and values keys in the failure JSON.
